title: Short Pull Workout with Dumbbell Curls

context.notes: Short late-night pull session followed by 15 minutes in a dry sauna. No numeric 0–6 readiness or pain ratings were supplied.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.notes: Eight total repetitions across two recorded sets. The five-repetition first set ties the existing best set. Because only two sets were recorded and strict form was not explicitly confirmed, this is not treated as a matched regression from longer sessions.

exercises.name: Two-Arm Cable Biceps Curl
exercises.notes: Normalized from ‘cable two arm curl.’ Attachment and cable-machine identity were not supplied.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.notes: Ten repetitions were performed at each listed load. Attachment and cable-machine identity were not supplied.

exercises.name: Reverse Cable Fly
exercises.notes: Per-side loading and execution style were not supplied. The entered stack value is preserved without doubling.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.notes: Fifteen pounds is recorded per dumbbell. Default volume preserves the entered per-side load without silently doubling it.

exercises.name: Spider Dumbbell Curl
exercises.notes: Twenty pounds is recorded per dumbbell. This establishes the first complete three-set spider-curl result at 20 lb: 10, 8, 8. Default volume preserves the entered per-side load without silently doubling it.

notes: Workout started at 10:00 PM local time on September 8 and lasted 40 minutes. It contained 16 completed sets, 136 completed repetitions, and 3,340 lb of preserved entered-load volume; the two bodyweight pull-up sets are excluded from external-load volume. A 15-minute dry sauna followed the workout and is recorded separately from lifting duration and volume. No RIR, pain, sleep, energy, soreness, or illness scores were supplied.
